title: SlashZero Demo
provenance: Reported by udance4ever (highball-db#939, 2026-11-03), Apple M1, macOS 27.2, Highball 0.10.24, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r29, D3DMetal, rated 1 of 5 after 1 minutes: the logo shows, then the game's own crash window ('The UE-Zero Game has crashed', Fatal error!) before the title screen. Not verified by the maintainer. udance4ever again in a comment on highball-db#939 (2026-11-03) with the game's own log: about a minute after start it stops on 'Unhandled Exception: 0xc06d007f', raised from kernelbase, the code for a delay-loaded function that wasn't found. udance4ever again in a comment on highball-db#939 (2026-11-04), in a Wine 11 environment on engine x64-crossover26.3-r28 with D3DMetal: no crash, but Steam shows a black window with white boxes, which the reporter takes for a licence agreement, and Highball keeps waiting for the game. Steam's helpers crash in that log ('-[NSViewBackingLayer setDisplaySyncEnabled:]: unrecognized selector'), Steam's window not drawing under D3DMetal. udance4ever again in a comment on highball-db#939 (2026-11-06): in the Wine 10 environment, with Steam started through Open Steam and the demo started from Steam's Play button, Unreal's message 'DirectX 12 is not supported on your system' came up. Steam started that way runs outside D3DMetal and the game inherits it, so it has no Direct3D 12 there, most likely the route rather than the game. udance4ever again in a comment on highball-db#939 (2026-11-06T21:00Z): in the Wine 11 environment, through Open Steam, no licence window showed and the demo never started. udance4ever again on highball-db#939 (2026-11-15), the Wine 11 environment: with the game's graphics mode set to DXMT for one launch, Steam's window drew and the licence agreement could be accepted, and with the mode back on D3DMetal the demo starts and plays. It defaults to the Ultra preset, Medium gives 20 to 30 fps and Low 40 to 60 fps on the M1. A DualSense works without Steam Input. While the demo ran, Highball said it never started, no process of its own appearing in six minutes. The demo starts in CrossOver too.
notes: Plays on a Wine 11 engine with D3DMetal on an M1 once Steam's licence agreement is accepted, Low at 40 to 60 fps and Medium at 20 to 30 (highball-db#939). On the Wine 10 engine it crashes after the logo with a Fatal error window. An Unreal Engine game on DirectX 12.

knownIssues.symptom: Unreal Engine 'Fatal error!' crash window right after the logo (M1, D3DMetal, Wine 10 r29)
knownIssues.cause: not diagnosed. The game's log ends with 'Unhandled Exception: 0xc06d007f', which is the code a program raises when a function it loads late from a DLL isn't there, so the game most likely asks one of Wine's DLLs for a function Wine doesn't have. Which one isn't known yet
knownIssues.fix: none known on Wine 10. A Wine 11 engine runs it (see below)

knownIssues.symptom: On a Wine 11 engine with D3DMetal, Steam shows a black window with white boxes at the first launch and the game never starts (M1, Wine 11 r28)
knownIssues.cause: Steam waits for the demo's licence agreement, and on the Wine 11 engines Steam's window can't draw under D3DMetal, so the agreement stays invisible. Through Open Steam it didn't show either (highball-db#939, 2026-11-06)
knownIssues.fix: the player's way (highball-db#939, 2026-11-15): set the game's graphics mode to DXMT on its page, press Play and accept the agreement in Steam's window, press Stop, set the mode back to D3DMetal and press Play again

knownIssues.symptom: Highball says the demo never started, no process of its own appearing in six minutes, while the game is running (M1, Wine 11)
knownIssues.cause: not diagnosed. Highball didn't recognise the game's process
knownIssues.fix: none needed to play, the game keeps running (highball-db#939)
